I reviewed all five passages in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-open-anesthesia-sim/70814b4a-8402-5228-b958-86946f315034/scratchpad/show3.txt. All five need a rewrite, and the rewrites are below. Four problems come first, because the rewrites cannot settle them.

**Check these before applying anything**
- **The 0.5% limit may already be gone.** Line 52 of the writing rule says the step-size test's 0.5% tolerance was "removed in `PL-VXM0`". All five passages describe it as still in force. For example, passage 2 says "The constants are in `tests/reference/test_sevo_patient.py`" and "0.5% becomes the working check". If the rule is right, these passages are out of date. Please check before applying any rewrite.
- **Passages 3 and 5 overlap.** They have the same bold lead, "The release check, and why it allows 0.5%", and mostly the same facts. Passages 1 and 4 also overlap: both give the earlier method's 0.04% (4e-4) gap and say the 0.5% (5e-3) is now only a coarse check. If both of a pair stand in one section, one repeats the other. The file has no rows marked "|", so I could not see where any passage stands. I also could not see whether passages 1, 2 and 4 sit inside a "**For developers.**" note. Their content belongs there.
- **The passages disagree on why 0.5% was chosen.** Passage 1 says no record says how it was chosen. Passage 3 says it "was set ... at about ten times the 0.04%", which reads as the reason. The rule forbids a reason that no record holds, and the rewrite of passage 3 fixes this.
- **I cannot tell what "below 1e-14 as a fraction" means.** In passage 1 it could be a gap relative to the value, or a plain difference in the agent's fraction of the gas. If it is relative, passage 4's measured gaps of about 1.4e-13 would fail it. I kept the words as they are.

[1] rewrite
```
- **Why 0.5%.** No record says how the 0.5% was chosen. It dates from an earlier, approximate
  method, whose 0.1 s and 0.025 s runs differed by about 0.04% in the alveolar concentration
  and by more in the mixed-venous concentration. The test that applies the 0.5% also requires
  each gap between two runs to stay below 1e-14 as a fraction. Because the test passes any gap
  of less than 1e-8, a gap that fails the 0.5% limit is at least 1e-8 and also fails the 1e-14
  limit. So today the 0.5% limit never decides whether the test passes.
```
- Words added (68 to about 95). They carry:
  - which runs differed: the 0.1 s and 0.025 s runs, from passages 4 and 5;
  - why a failing gap is at least 1e-8: the test passes any gap of less than 1e-8, from passage 4;
  - what a gap is: "between two runs";
  - "the test that applies the 0.5%", which gives "the same test" a noun to point at.
- Restated: "it was chosen" becomes "the 0.5% was chosen", "breaks" becomes "fails", "changes no outcome" becomes "never decides whether the test passes", and "mixed venous" becomes "the mixed-venous concentration".
- If this bullet is the developer note for passage 5's section, it can also take the facts moved out of passages 3 and 5. They are listed at the end of this report.

[3] rewrite
```
**The release check, and why it allows 0.5%.** The model advances in fixed steps of 0.1 s,
and a shorter step should give almost the same result. Before each release, a test reruns the
first minute of the default sevoflurane induction with steps of 0.1 s, 0.05 s and 0.025 s.
Each run's alveolar, vessel-rich and mixed-venous concentrations must be within 0.5% of the run
with the next shorter step. A compartment that holds almost no agent also passes if its values
in the two runs differ by less than 0.000001 vol%, because in such a compartment a tiny
difference is a large percentage. The 0.5% dates from the simulator's earlier calculation
method. The current method's runs agree to better than one part in a trillion (measured
2026-10-03), so the much tighter limits in the paragraphs above are the ones that would catch
a real error.
```
- Moved: "at about ten times the 0.04% alveolar difference that method showed" goes to the "**For developers.**" note at the end of this section (wording at the end of this report).
- Reordered: the near-empty-compartment sentence now follows the 0.5% rule, so both conditions of the check come before the reason for the 0.5%.
- Restated: "was set for" becomes "dates from", "its two values" becomes "its values in the two runs", "there" becomes "in such a compartment", and "above" becomes "in the paragraphs above".
